content.value_statement: Teams often configure AI agents with inconsistent tool access. This skill provides reusable preset groups for development, analysis, research, file operations, and orchestration.
actual_capabilities: Defines named presets for development, file operations, analysis, research, orchestration, and full-stack agents.
Lists included tools for each documented preset, including Read, Write, Edit, Bash, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task, and TodoWrite.
Provides selection guidance for when each preset should be used.
Includes a YAML frontmatter example for applying a preset pattern to an agent.
Links to separate reference files with detailed tool lists and example agents.
limitations: Does not enforce tool permissions automatically; users must configure their agent platform.
Does not validate whether a preset is safe for a specific project.
Does not provide runtime policy controls, approval workflows, or auditing.
The full-stack preset is broad and should be restricted in sensitive environments.

use_cases.title: Maintain Agent Libraries
use_cases.description: Create consistent tool access profiles for many Claude Code agents.

use_cases.title: Assign Development Work
use_cases.description: Choose a preset before giving build, test, or refactoring work to an AI agent.

use_cases.title: Separate Research Duties
use_cases.description: Keep web research agents separate from agents that can execute local commands.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Preset
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent purpose and recommend one tool-presets preset. Explain why it fits and name any permission risks.

prompt_templates.title: Map Agent Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: For these agent roles, assign a tool-presets preset to each role. Keep privileges minimal and flag roles that need Bash or web access.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Tool Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current tools for this agent against the matching tool-presets preset. Identify extra permissions, missing permissions, and safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Design Preset Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tool access policy using tool-presets for development, research, and orchestration agents. Include approval rules for Bash, web access, and full-stack use.

output_examples.input: Agent role: documentation updater that searches files and edits Markdown.
output_examples.output: Recommended preset: file-ops. It supports file search and editing without shell execution.

output_examples.input: Agent role: dependency auditor that must run package audit commands.
output_examples.output: Recommended preset: analysis. It supports reading, searching, and diagnostic commands through Bash.

output_examples.input: Agent role: multi-step project coordinator that delegates tasks.
output_examples.output: Recommended preset: orchestration. It supports task delegation and progress tracking, but should not run shell commands directly.

best_practices: Choose the narrowest preset that supports the agent workflow.
Require review before assigning Bash, web access, Task, or full-stack capabilities.
Keep each agent description aligned with the preset tools it receives.
anti_patterns: Assigning full-stack access to agents that only need file search or editing.
Using a research preset for tasks that require verified local code execution.
Copying preset names without configuring the actual tool permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It documents reusable tool access presets for common Claude Code agent types.

faq.question: Does it change permissions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that users must apply in their agent configuration.

faq.question: Which preset is safest for file updates?
faq.answer: The file-ops preset is safer when shell execution is not required.

faq.question: When should I use the analysis preset?
faq.answer: Use it for code review, static analysis, security scanning, and diagnostic tasks.

faq.question: Why is full-stack access risky?
faq.answer: It grants broad capabilities and can exceed the permissions needed for a specific task.

faq.question: Can this work with Codex and Claude?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.
